p:cNvPr.descr: The process and materials for protein purification. At the top is the gene for target protein, which is labeled below. It is represented by a long, thin bar. It is red in the center and light blue on either end. Below is a down arrow with a convergent arrow to the right showing the addition of the gene for GST (labeled below), which is a long, thin bar which is purple in the center and light blue on either end. The down arrow points down to the fused gene, labeled “gene for fusion protein”, which is a long, thin rectangle that is light blue on the end, then red, then purple, then blue on the far right end. The end of the leftmost light blue section has a right arrow on top labeled “transcription.” A down arrow below points to an image of a cell, which is a simple irregular circle shaded yellow, with the blue mass of genetic material on the left side. A small section of the genetic material has been shaded red. An arrow pointing to the right indicates 4 proteins synthesized by the fused gene. These proteins consist of a red sphere bonded right to a purple sphere with a round cutout on the right side. A text box to the right reads, “Express fusion protein in the cell.” Below this is a down arrow with a text box to the right reading, “Prepare cell extract containing fusion protein as part of the cell protein mixture.” The arrow points down to a beaker which contains a clear fluid with a blue tube traveling up and to the left; the clear fluid has brown, red, purple, and yellow protein fragments floating in it. To the left of this is a text box reading, “Protein mixture is added to the column.” The blue tube travels up and through a tan box to the upper right labeled “pump”, then down into a tall column. The top of the column is red and black and connects with the tube; the bottom is also red and black. The middle of the tube is clear with a gray medium inside. Inside the tube the proteins have been separated. The brown and yellow proteins have settled toward the bottom end of the tube; the purple and red proteins float toward the top. There is a small box around some of the purple and red proteins; this magnifies forward and left to show microscopic interactions inside the tube. The red and purple proteins are shown attached to the surface of a large gray sphere with light green oval-shaped protrusions on its surface. The green protrusions are labeled, “Glutathione anchored to medium binds GST tag”; the purple protein is labeled “GST tag.” To the right and left of the GST tags bound to the medium, two arrows point down to the yellow and brown proteins, which are anchored to nothing. Below the proteins are shown dripping into 9 lined-up test tubes; the brown and yellow proteins have dripped out of the tube and into tubes 3 and 4. Below is a text box reading, “Other proteins flow through the column.” An arrow to the right points to a second process. At the top of the image is another beaker, this time full of a clear fluid with green proteins floating inside. There is a text box to the left reading, “Solution of free glutathione is added to column.” A blue tube travels up from the beakers, right through a tan box labeled “pump” and down into the tube. Inside the tube is the gray medium with just the glutathione anchored to the GST tags at the bottom of the tube. A small box around a gray area inside the tube magnifies forward and to the left to a larger box, which has the gray sphere with the green protrusions and no GST tags bonded to it. Below the tube, this mixture drips into test tube 7, and contains the glutathione (green) with the GST tag (purple + red). Below is a text box reading, “Fusion protein is eluted by glutathione solution.”
